initial.title: [v0.92.1][AWS-B] AWS access and billing baseline
initial.goal: Produce one accepted AWS access and billing control baseline for the approved Agent Logic business AWS account.
initial.required_outcome: A reviewed access and billing baseline with independently recoverable corporate administration, governed Agent Toolkit access, read-only default agent posture, CloudWatch and CloudTrail attribution, visible billing ownership, budgets, anomaly handling, export, and cost attribution without removing the proven administrator path.
authority_boundary: Issue #485 owns only the AWS access and billing baseline.
Issue #484 owns the accepted AWS resource ownership inventory predecessor.
Issue #486 owns AWS Terraform bootstrap after this baseline is accepted.
Issue #122 continues to own public WSS, Route53, ACM, and public exposure topology.
No AWS Organizations rollout, workload deployment, administrator removal, Terraform apply, resource cleanup, unrestricted agent mutation, or production traffic change is authorized by #485.
AWS mutation is not performed unless a typed issue lane explicitly records the exact approved operation and operator approval boundary.
operator_constraints: Use the Agent Logic business AWS profile agent-logic-admin, not a personal/default profile.
Do not print, copy, commit, or expose AWS credential material.
Default AWS evidence collection to read-only commands.
Preserve existing administrator access until replacement is independently proven.
Keep work in the existing FastWork issue worktree and preserve #122, #554, and #490 lanes.
Obtain fresh exact-head review before publication.
initial.task_boundary: Exactly one accepted access-and-billing baseline; individual readbacks are evidence inputs and do not close independently.
deliverables: Human, workload, and agent-initiated identity census
Agent Toolkit for AWS approved Codex path and AWS CLI version check
Agent IAM guardrail and read-only default posture specification
Billing, budget, anomaly, export, and cost-attribution readbacks
Credential redaction and no-mutation validation proof
Fresh exact-head review and closing PR
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Corporate recovery does not depend on one personal factor.
AC-2: Human workload and agent-initiated identities are distinguishable.
AC-3: Agent Toolkit for AWS is configured for the approved Codex path with AWS CLI 2.35 or newer.
AC-4: IAM context policies bind agent actions with read-only default posture.
AC-5: CloudWatch metrics and CloudTrail requests are attributable.
AC-6: Billing and budget ownership is visible.
AC-7: Existing administrator access remains until replacement is proven.
AC-8: Evidence contains no credentials, secrets, raw token contents, or unintended mutation commands.
AC-9: Fresh exact-head review has zero actionable findings and publication truth closes only issue #485.
initial.plan_summary: Bootstrap #485 from current origin/main after #484 PR #556 merge, preserve the accepted AWS-A inventory as dependency input, capture a redacted AWS access and billing baseline, validate local redaction/no-mutation and coverage, obtain fresh review, then publish one closing PR.

steps.action: Confirm #484 live closure and current main ancestry, then bootstrap and bind #485 in the existing FastWork worktree.
Verify approved account identity and AWS CLI version without printing credentials.
Record corporate recovery, identity census, and administrator-continuity baseline.
Record Agent Toolkit, agent IAM guardrail, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, billing, budget, anomaly, export, and cost-attribution readbacks.
Validate redaction, no-mutation posture, diff hygiene, and lifecycle truth; obtain fresh exact-head review and publish.

invariants: Existing administrator access remains in place until replacement is proven.
Human, workload, and agent identities remain distinguishable.
Agent access defaults to read-only unless a later operator-approved lane proves otherwise.
Billing/cost evidence is visible without exposing sensitive payment data.
Downstream AWS-C and deferred #122 scope remain separate.
risks: The active AWS profile could point at the wrong account.
Billing APIs may require payer/root permissions that are not available to the read-only profile.
Some audit readbacks may lag CloudTrail or CloudWatch ingestion.
Agent Toolkit setup could imply AWS resource creation if not constrained to documentation/configuration and read-only checks.
Evidence could accidentally include sensitive ARNs, account IDs, payment metadata, or command history.
stop_conditions: Replacement access is unproven and a change would remove existing administrator access.
A required AWS operation would mutate state without explicit typed approval.
Fresh review finds unresolved actionable issues.

validation_lanes.proof_role: Record corporate recovery posture without removing existing administrator access.
Read back human, workload, and agent-visible IAM identities without credential disclosure.
Verify AWS CLI 2.35 or newer and record the approved Agent Toolkit for AWS Codex path.
Verify agent IAM read-only default posture and context policy documentation.
Verify CloudWatch and CloudTrail attribution readbacks for the configured profile and agent path.
Verify billing ownership, budget, anomaly, export, and cost-attribution readbacks.
Reject credential material and unintended mutation verbs in retained AWS-B evidence.
Prove current typed issue integrity before exact-head review and closing publication.

initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on account ambiguity, billing-target ambiguity, required unapproved mutation, credential exposure, administrator-removal risk, scope drift, stale review, or red CI.
review_prompts: Is #484 dependency truth accurately represented without re-owning AWS-A inventory scope?
Does the baseline prove recovery, identity separation, agent guardrails, audit attribution, and billing visibility from retained evidence?
Does the Agent Toolkit section avoid authorizing unbounded AWS mutation?
Are credentials, payment data, and secret material excluded from retained evidence?
Are #486 and #122 scopes clearly out of bounds?
initial.review_scope: Issue #485 docs, evidence, lifecycle truth, access/billing baseline, readback scripts, redaction proof, and exact branch range.
